title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-breadcrumbs-2
content:
Goal: capture quick breadcrumbs / commands tried while debugging capacity thrash and warmup failures in dedicated GPU pool scheduling. Mostly notes-to-self and things for follow-up with SRE/infra.

Summary of problem observed:
- Customer-facing latency spikes and 503s during morning traffic spike (around 09:12-09:35 UTC).
- Autoscaler repeatedly adds nodes then drains them quickly -> observed as capacity thrash. Warmup (docker image + python package cache) not completing before scheduler routes real traffic.
- Affected pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-prod-us-west2 (4 x A100 pools, mixed node types - some 80GB, some 40GB).

Quick timeline notes (local timestamps):
- 09:09: first steady increase in queue length (avg queue depth up 3x).
- 09:12: autoscaler scaled from 16 -> 20 nodes. New nodes registered but readiness_probes slow (image pull ~45s, init scripts ~20s).
- 09:15: scheduler placed pods onto new nodes and started traffic. Not all warmup hooks finished -> cold starts for a subset of requests.
- 09:18: observed oom/killed? No, but infra reported node underutilized for first 30s then heavy. Autoscaler then considered these nodes underutilized and scheduled scale-down attempts (scale-down TTL too short?).
- 09:27: scale-down attempt collided with ongoing warmups -> nodes drained and removed while remaining requests were still hitting others -> cascade.

Concrete logs / errors captured:
- kube-scheduler logs (snippet):
  E1105 09:15:12.345678 1 binder.go:245] Failed to bind pod default/inference-worker-abc123: node(s) had taint {uninitialized: true}, that the pod didn't tolerate
- autoscaler logs (snippet):
  INFO 2024-11-05T09:17:21Z autoscaler.go: Scaling up: desired=20 current=16 reason="queue > target threshold"
  DEBUG 2024-11-05T09:17:45Z node_lifecycle.go: Node warmup not complete: node=node-24 image_pull_progress=75% warmup_hook_status=running
  WARN 2024-11-05T09:26:02Z scaler.go: Candidate for scale-down: node-24 last_active=160s low_util=true
- serving runtime logs (partial):
  WARN runtime/warmup: kv-cache warmup incomplete for model gpt-large, keys_loaded=12000/50000
  ERROR runtime/requests: inference failed: backend busy -> 503 returned to client

Commands I ran during investigation (local)
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels | grep node-24
- kubectl describe node node-24 (checked taints: uninitialized, gpu.present)
- kubectl logs -n infra autoscaler-0 --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p' > autoscaler-09-17.log
- kubectl get pods -n inference -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,NODE:.spec.nodeName -l app=inference | grep Warmup
- ssh ops@node-24 sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2024-11-05 09:00" | grep -i warmup
- curl -s http://metrics.internal/export?metric=queue_depth&from=2024-11-05T09:00Z&to=2024-11-05T09:40Z > q.csv

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Race between autoscaler scale-down TTL and warmup duration. TTL too short (default 2m) so nodes get considered for scale-down before warmup completes.
2) Warmup hooks are not blocking readiness/probes. Pods become Ready before runtime warmup finishes (kubelet readiness vs app-level warmup). Scheduler routes traffic to pods that are "Ready" but not warm.
3) Image pull + package installs are causing variable boot times on some node families (40GB vs 80GB have different image cache hit rates) leading autoscaler to misinterpret short-term low utilization.
4) Taints/tolerations mismatch: some warmup pods have uninitialized taint handling, causing scheduling delays and then mass scheduling when taints removed -> bursty placement.
5) Batching heuristics in runtime assume warm KV-cache data across nodes; cold nodes cause many small batched requests -> increased per-token latency and perceived low throughput -> autoscaler misreads metrics.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses:
- Check scale-down TTL config in autoscaler configmap (k8s-autoscaler-config) and compare to observed warmup_time distribution (metric: runtime.warmup_duration).
- Confirm that readinessProbe is tied to actual warmup state (e.g., /healthz returns 200 only after kv-cache loaded).
- Inspect node image cache hit metrics (node_image_cache_hit_ratio) across node types for last 7 days.
- Look for taint/toleration churn events in audit logs around 09:10-09:20.

Immediate mitigations attempted (notes):
- Increased scale-down TTL from 120s -> 300s in test pool (k8s-autoscaler-config) and observed lower thrash in replay runs. Needs prod rollout discussion.
- Added temporary gate: mark pods NotReady until warmup hook completes (patched readiness endpoint in canary). Early canary shows fewer 503s but longer tail latencies for some requests (expected).
- Pre-pulled docker image on a subset of nodes via DaemonSet to test image pull impact (results: 15-25s faster start on those nodes).

Repro steps (how to reproduce locally / in staging)
1) Create synthetic traffic spike script (loadgen) that submits N concurrent short chats and forces model gpt-large to cold kernel path.
2) Reset image cache on a few nodes (ssh wipe /var/lib/docker/image/overlay2/*) or use small node pool with no cached images.
3) Ensure autoscaler thresholds configured same as prod.
4) Run loadgen and watch for: nodes added, readiness reported, node scale-down events overlapping warmup.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- What is the exact metric autoscaler uses to pick scale-down candidates? cpu_util? gpu_util? pod_count? Need to confirm and consider switching to a GPU-utilization-aware metric.
- Can we hook warmup completion into the cluster autoscaler (e.g., do not consider node for scale-down until a label warmup=done present)?
- Should warmup be done pre-scheduling (startup probe) instead of readiness? Pros/cons: blocks scheduling but avoids traffic to cold pods.
- Is there a way for runtime to advertise expected warmup time to autoscaler as a hint? (e.g., prometheus metric warmup_remaining_seconds)

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Sync with SRE (Marcus) and infra (Priya) about increasing scale-down TTL in prod for morning traffic window. Link: INF-482.
- [ ] Add a short-lived scale-in blocker label when warmup starts (prototype using mutating webhook) - low effort POC.
- [ ] Add runtime metric runtime.warmup_duration and runtime.warmup_complete{node=} to Prometheus; alert on slow warmups.
- [ ] Sweep node image cache strategy: pre-warm images for preferred node families; consider DaemonSet pre-pull for peak windows.
- [ ] Draft runbook entry: "Dedicated pool warmup thrash" with playbook to increase TTL, patch readiness, and scale policy rollback steps.

Notes to self: save the autoscaler logs, node journal, and kube-apiserver audit for 09:00-09:40 UTC. Correlate with console traces for top 5 customer requests that got 503.

Related tickets / reference:
- INF-482 (prod incident) -> notes in Confluence (link in linked_artifacts)
- infra PR #789: autoscaler config defaults tweak (test-only)

If I forget: primary suspected root cause = "scale-down too aggressive relative to warmup time + readiness not tied to warmup". Workflow: ensure readiness blocks until warmup, or increase TTL / avoid scale-down until label present.

End of scratchpad.
